decisions.reason: Through-hole assembly does not change the specified connector locations, alignment, accessibility, or straight-versus-right-angle orientations.
The source decision does not change the legacy BOM completeness rule or the optional population status of the two connectors.
A through-hole connector choice does not alter the requirement to provide a complete, board-specific sensor-board BOM.
Through-hole assembly is independent of the power-board connectors' placement, accessibility, mounting-hole clearance, and right-angle orientation requirements.
The source selects connector assembly technology but does not change the interboard connector families, pinouts, references, or power and signal roles.
Connector assembly style does not necessarily change the power board's dimensions, mounting arrangement, installation orientation, or USB-C edge placement.

Accepting the higher through-hole connector cost for the development boards constrains the design but does not revoke or modify the existing general cost-optimization goal or component-selection policy.
The ESP32 breakout is already explicitly through-hole, so the source decision introduces no change to its current state.
The source does not change the power-board BOM's part-number completeness or design-justification requirements.
Connector assembly style does not alter the required sensor-board fabrication and placement export set.
The requirement for connector pin markings remains valid unchanged regardless of whether the connectors use through-hole assembly.
The connector assembly decision does not affect resolution or portability of the L1 inductor footprint.
